```{r}

# Import Colonnade Connections Data
connections_data <- read.csv("connections.csv")

# Installing packages and libraries
install.packages("readxl")
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)

# Rename column names within connections_data
colnames(connections_data)[6] <- "Major" 
colnames(connections_data)[1] <- "Alum_ID" 
colnames(connections_data)[2] <- "Class" 
colnames(connections_data)[3] <- "Industry" 
colnames(connections_data)[7] <- "Minor" 
colnames(connections_data)[8] <- "Greek_Org"
colnames(connections_data)[10] <- "Activities" 

View(connections_data)

```

```{r}
#Make a "city", "state" column within connections_data
connections_data <- connections_data %>%
 unite("City_State", City, State, sep = ", ",) %>% 
  
#Changing Arlington, VA to Washington, DC
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Arlington, VA", "Washington, DC", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Brooklyn, NY", "New York, NY", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Washington Dc, DC", "Washington, DC", City_State))%>%
  mutate(City_State = ifelse(City_State == "Washington D.C., DC", "Washington, DC", City_State))%>%
  
```


```{r}
  #New Columns for multiple sports in connections_data
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = Sports,
    delim  = "; ",
    names = c("Sport_1", "Sport_2", "Sport_3"),
    too_few = "align_start",
    too_many = "drop",
    cols_remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  #new Column for double major
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = Major,
    delim  = "; ",
    names = c("Major", "Major_2"),
    too_few = "align_start",
    too_many = "drop",
    cols_remove = TRUE
  )

# Factor columns in connections_data
connections_data$Major <- factor(connections_data$Major)
connections_data$City_State <- factor(connections_data$City_State)
connections_data$Class <- factor(connections_data$Class)
connections_data$Industry <- factor(connections_data$Industry)
connections_data$Minor <- factor(connections_data$Minor)
connections_data$Greek_Org <- factor(connections_data$Greek_Org)
connections_data$Sports <- factor(connections_data$Sports)


View(connections_data)
```

```{r}
#Create City Summary table based on Connections data
#How many alumni in each city

city_summary <- connections_data %>%
  group_by(City_State) %>%
  summarise(
    Alumni_Count = n_distinct(Alum_ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Alumni_Count))

View(city_summary)


```

```{r}

#Create City Greek Org table based on Connections data
#How many alumni in each greek org in each city
city_greekOrg <- connections_data %>%
  group_by(City_State, Greek_Org) %>%
  summarise(
    Alumni_Count = n_distinct(Alum_ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(City_State, desc(Alumni_Count))

```

```{r}
#Create City Sport table based on Connections data
#How many alumni who played each sport in each city
city_sport <- connections_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Sport_1, Sport_2, Sport_3),
    names_to = "Sport_Column",
    values_to = "Sport"
  )%>%
  filter(!is.na(Sport), Sport != "") %>%
  distinct(Alum_ID, City_State, Sport) %>%
  group_by(City_State, Sport) %>%
  summarise(
    Alumni_Count = n_distinct(Alum_ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(City_State, desc(Alumni_Count))

View(city_sport)

```


```{r}
# Import and clean Labor Market Tightness Index dataset


# 2. Import Labor Market Tightness dataset
labor_market_tightness <- read_excel(
  "labor_market_tightness_index.xlsx")
  show_col_types = FALSE

  
# 3. Create reference table matching W&L's top 30 cities to their names in the original dataset
city_lookup <- tribble(
  ~City_State,           ~source_metro,
  "New York, NY",        "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ",
  "Washington, DC",      "Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV",
  "Atlanta, GA",         "Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell, GA",
  "Charlotte, NC",       "Charlotte-Concord-Gastonia, NC-SC",
  "Dallas, TX",          "Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX",
  "Houston, TX",         "Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands, TX",
  "Richmond, VA",        "Richmond, VA",
  "Austin, TX",          "Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX",
  "Charlottesville, VA", "Charlottesville, VA",
  "Lexington, VA",       NA_character_,
  "Nashville, TN",       "Nashville-Davidson--Murfreesboro--Franklin, TN",
  "Chicago, IL",         "Chicago-Naperville-Elgin, IL-IN",
  "Alexandria, VA",      "Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV",
  "Raleigh, NC",         "Raleigh-Cary, NC",
  "Philadelphia, PA",    "Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD",
  "Charleston, SC",      "Charleston-North Charleston, SC",
  "San Francisco, CA",   "San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, CA",
  "Baltimore, MD",       "Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, MD",
  "Henrico, VA",         "Richmond, VA",
  "Boston, MA",          "Boston-Cambridge-Newton, MA-NH",
  "Denver, CO",          "Denver-Aurora-Centennial, CO",
  "Durham, NC",          "Durham-Chapel Hill, NC",
  "New Orleans, LA",     "New Orleans-Metairie, LA",
  "Roanoke, VA",         "Roanoke, VA",
  "Birmingham, AL",      "Birmingham, AL",
  "Pittsburgh, PA",      "Pittsburgh, PA",
  "Cincinnati, OH",      "Cincinnati, OH-KY-IN",
  "Fort Worth, TX",      "Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX",
  "Greenville, SC",      "Greenville-Anderson-Greer, SC",
  "Tampa, FL",           "Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater, FL"
)


# 4. Filter and standardize dataset
labor_tightness_clean <- city_lookup |>
  filter(!is.na(source_metro)) |>      # filter() to exclude cities without a source metro
  inner_join(                            
    labor_market_tightness,
    by = join_by(source_metro == City_State)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Identify destinations using a shared metro value
    metro_proxy = City_State %in% c(
      "Alexandria, VA",
      "Henrico, VA",
      "Fort Worth, TX"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    City_State,
    Tightness_Index,
    cbsa_code,
    Rank,
    source_metro,
    metro_proxy
  )

```
